newsitem.title: PERU: Mourners hold mass at sea for Peru crash victims.
newsitem.headline: Mourners hold mass at sea for Peru crash victims.

text.p: Hundreds of mourners held a mass on Saturday in the Pacific Ocean off Peru's coast where a Boeing 757-200 crashed this week killing all 70 on board.

Catholic Bishop Miguel Irizar, from the port of El Callao where the Peruvian navy frigate left, led the ceremony as relatives of the victims scattered flowers on the surface of the sea about 95 miles (150 km) northwest of the coast off Lima.
Most of the relatives were from Chile, which lost 30 people in Wednesday's tragedy. Peruvians, Mexicans and Ecuadoreans were also on board to mourn their victims.
The 70 dead also included passengers from the United States, Italy, Great Britain, New Zealand, Spain, Colombia and Venezuela.

A navy-led team of helicopters, frigates and private boats scouring the crash site since dawn on Wednesday, continued to search the waters for bodies and debris but by early on Saturday afternoon, only 14 bodies had been recovered.
The majority of the other dead passengers were still trapped 180 yards (180 metres) below the surface in the fusilage of the plane.
Aeroperu officials said a private U.S. company had been contracted to help reach the main body of the plane and extract the "black box" flight recorder and remaining corpses.

The Peruvian government has pinned the blame for the accident on technical faults which it said made the computers aboard the plane "go crazy," leaving pilot Eric Schreiber without instruments as he struggled to return through dense fog to Lima after taking off for the Chilean capital of Santiago.
A 12-member investigative team from Boeing, engine maker Pratt & Whitney, the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transporation Safety Board, has so far reserved judgment.
Boeing representatives insist it is premature to determine the cause of the crash.

Wednesday's accident, one of the worst in Peru's aviation history, came seven months after a Boeing 737 belonging to local Faucett airline crashed and killed all 123 people on board near Peru's second city, Arequipa.
Since 1967, a total of 601 people have been killed in air crashes in Peru.
